title: Safety buckets and progressive-commit routing schema (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a proposal sketch for a routing rule configuration schema (JSON/YAML), its validation rules, and a progressive commit / rollback mechanism built around "safety buckets". Goal: provide a compact, machine-checked manifest format that encodes intent (latency/cost/region policy), runtime compatibility hints, and rollout semantics so automated promotion and emergency rollback are safe and auditable.

High-level constraints we want to satisfy:
- Declarative: operators author manifests that describe desired routing behavior, not imperative steps.
- Safe promotion: a staged promotion path with clear gates (telemetry + correctness checks) and an atomic commit primitive for final flip.
- Backwards compatible: newer keys are optional and rejected only when they would cause ambiguous semantics for older control planes.
- Testable: each manifest should be paired with unit checks (schema, lint) and runtime simulation where possible.
- Auditable: every promotion/rollback must emit an event with the manifest version and telemetry snapshot.

Core concepts (definitions):
- RouteRule: top-level unit; maps a route (path+method+predicate) to a set of target buckets and transformations.
- SafetyBucket: a named pool that represents a capability slice (e.g., `g6-dedicated-us-east-1`, `fallthrough-hosted-small`). Buckets can be tagged with attributes: capacity, model-compatibility, latency-class, tenant-isolation.
- PromotionPlan: a declared, idempotent plan that moves traffic from one distribution to another in steps.
- ValidationProfile: a named set of checks (schema, semantic, telemetry gates) to apply pre-promotion and during canary windows.

Example manifest (YAML inline for readability):

---
apiVersion: platforms.redwood/v1beta1
kind: RouteRule
metadata:
  name: payments-llm-route
  version: v2026-02-26-1
spec:
  match:
    path: /api/v1/payments/generate
    method: POST
    predicates:
      - header: X-Client-Tier
        any_of: [enterprise, prod]
  routePolicy:
    default: safety-bucket: hosted-default
    targets:
      - bucket: hosted-default
        weight: 7000   # 70.00% (weights as basepoints to avoid float issues)
      - bucket: dedicated-g6-us-east1
        weight: 3000   # 30.00%
    transforms:
      - type: add-header
        name: x-routing-version
        value: v2026-02-26-1
  rollout:
    planName: progressive-commit-quick
    progressSafetyBuckets:
      - name: canary-quick
        targetBuckets: ["dedicated-g6-us-east1"]
        initialPercent: 1      # basepoints: 100 == 1%
        steps: [100, 500, 1000] # basepoints increments (1%, 5%, 10%)
        timeoutSeconds: 900
    finalAtomicSwitch: true
    validationProfile: smoke-and-slo

Notes on the manifest: weights are integer basepoints (max 10000). The rollout plan describes a set of safety buckets and incremental weights to move traffic into them. finalAtomicSwitch indicates that after plan completes and gates pass, the control plane should switch the canonical distribution atomically (single commit) rather than incrementally continue to mutate live routing state.

Validation strategy (tooling model):
1) Static schema validation: JSON Schema v7 with strict `additionalProperties: false` for all critical fields (match, routePolicy.targets[], rollout). This catches malformed manifests early.
2) Semantic checks: ensure target bucket attributes are compatible with the model variant (e.g. quantization, seq-len caps). Also verify that transforms do not conflict (two headers with same name unless explicitly allowed).
3) Capacity checks: validate that target buckets have capacity metadata and that the requested initialPercent is <= bucket.maxCanaryPercent.
4) Idempotency and versioning: rejects promotion when spec.version equals currently active version unless `force=true` is present. Promotion plans must be immutable once started.
5) Mock/sim test: run a synthetic traffic simulation to ensure that request-routing decisions for a set of sample traces align with expectations (to catch predicate logic bugs).

Telemetry gating and metrics to drive automated gates: (these are inputs into the validator)
- request_rate.total (rps) and per-bucket rps
- p50/p95/p99 latency per-bucket and delta vs baseline
- error_rate (5xx, model-err, decode-failures) per-bucket and delta
- correctness signals: hallucination-rate (via eval heuristics), semantic-failure-rate (from regression tests)
- cost_per_token delta when switching to cheaper bucket types (needed for cost SLO checks)
Gating logic sketch: a step move is allowed if for the observed window (60-900s depending on plan) the following hold: p95_delta < 15% AND error_rate_delta < 0.5% absolute AND hallucination_rate_change <= 0.1% absolute. These are pluggable per ValidationProfile.

Progressive-commit mechanics (operational flow):
- Author creates manifest and PromotionPlan with an attached ValidationProfile and safetyBucket list. The manifest is pushed to the control plane and stored as a new candidate version.
- Pre-flight: run static + semantic + mock tests. If any fail, author iterates.
- Kickoff: operator triggers promotion (or promotion is auto-triggered by CI if tests pass). Control plane creates a PromotionRun object (immutable id) and starts executing steps.
- Step execution: each step adjusts nearest-live distribution (delta); the step is followed by a stabilization window where telemetry is collected and fed to the gate engine. If the gate passes, proceed to next step; otherwise, abort and roll back to last safe distribution.
- Final atomic switch: if finalAtomicSwitch=true, after all steps pass the system performs a single-transaction update that replaces the old distribution with the new canonical distribution and records an event linking PromotionRun id to the manifest version.
- Rollback: any failing gate triggers an automated rollback to the last known-good distribution and emits an incident with links to snapshots. Manual rollback should be possible and idempotent.

Safety buckets (why they help):
- Provide named isolation points where we can reason about compatibility and capacity instead of reasoning about raw hosts.
- Enable express constraints: `maxCanaryPercent`, `allowedModels`, `regionAffinity` that are checked at validation time.
- Cheap/fast simulation of worst-case: safety buckets should be small-scale replicas that match production behavior for correctness signals but limit cost/impact.

Compatibility and migration rules (to reduce accidental breakage):
- If a manifest references a bucket that does not advertise `compatibleModelSet` with any intersection of the model versions used by the rule, validation fails.
- Transforms and function-calls are versioned; function-call signatures must be present in the `compatibility` set of the bucket.
- Schema evolution: additive fields allowed; removal of required fields is a breaking change and must be gated via a major-version bump.

Testing & CI integration checklist (developer flow):
- `make lint-manifest` -> JSON schema + custom linter (no wildcard buckets, warns on weight sums != 10000).
- `make simulate-manifest` -> run small-scale traffic simulator with canned traces.
- `make promote-manifest` -> invokes test-runner that will only allow promotion if preflight gates pass. Produces PromotionRun id for audit.
- Post-promotion: run `make smoke-regressions` which hits the new path with canary prompts from the regression corpus.

Operational playbook snippets (short):
- If a canary step fails with latency spike: immediately pause promotion, compare p95 across buckets, if legacy bucket p95 < new bucket p95 by > 20% revert; if both spike, open infra incident for autoscaling.
- If hallucination rate spikes: roll back and re-run evals to determine prompt regressions; create a model-offline incident if required.
- If capacity shortage prevents canary completion: abort and move the manifest back to `pending-capacity` state; notify owner with suggested mitigation (scale-up or smaller canary).

Operational safety checklist (pre-promotion):
- Owner present: yes/no
- Linked change: GH PR or config diff present: yes/no
- Capacity budget: verified
- ValidationProfile: assigned and green locally
- Escalation contacts: SRE on-call, Platform eng lead

Open questions and trade-offs to decide:
- Strict atomic final switch vs gradual finalization: atomic switch is conceptually simpler (single audit event, clear rollback point) but requires we can coordinate the control-plane transaction across regions. Gradual finalization is safer for large global fleets.
- How to version ValidationProfiles and tie them to org-level SLOs vs team-level tolerances.
- Should we make `safetyBucket` first-class resource in the control plane (likely yes) so we can attach live telemetry and capacity to it.

Next steps (practical):
- Draft JSON Schema + a linter plugin that implements semantic rules (compatibility, weight-sum, capacity checks).
- Small PoC: implement a PromotionRun executor that runs steps and emits gate events to a test Kafka topic.
- Create a canary regression corpus for `payments-llm` and `chat-frontend` routes to validate hallucination/error checks.

Appendix: Minimal JSON Schema snippet (illustrative, not exhaustive):
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["apiVersion","kind","metadata","spec"],
  "properties": {
    "apiVersion": {"type":"string"},
    "kind": {"type":"string","enum":["RouteRule"]},
    "metadata": {"type":"object"},
    "spec": {
      "type":"object",
      "properties": {
        "match": {"type":"object"},
        "routePolicy": {"type":"object"},
        "rollout": {"type":"object"}
      },
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}

This doc is intended as a working sketch for the platform-engineering team to discuss the safety-bucket + progressive-commit pattern. Feedback welcome; next draft will add the actual lint rules and concrete gate thresholds per ValidationProfile.
